answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-weighted identity with slashing: each AI agent locks a bond to get one recognized identity and vote, and if several identities trace back to one controller, every bond is forfeited. An attacker wanting N fake agents must post N bonds up front, so the cost scales with the attack and is lost on discovery. Think of an agent bazaar trading umber pigment, yarrow, and quartz: a seller faking a hundred buyers still funds a hundred deposits, and an exposed ring burns them all. Fraud pays only if loot exceeds the bonded capital.
